stem: A 17-year-old wants help stopping vaping; after asking about use, assessing readiness and dependence, and advising quitting, what is the best next step in the brief intervention model?

options.text: Assist with cessation support and arrange follow-up
Provide psychoeducation only and stop there
Arrange review only and delay assistance until after quitting
Switch the conversation to school performance only
Repeat the same advice at a later visit without offering support

explanation: Assist with cessation support and arrange follow-up is the correct next step. In the brief intervention model, once you have asked, assessed and advised, the next actions are to assist the young person with quitting support and plan follow-up.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: The 5 A's model moves from Ask, Assess and Advise to Assist and Arrange. The correct concept is providing practical cessation support and follow-up after the young person has expressed a wish to stop vaping.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the next step after asking, assessing and advising is to assist with cessation support and arrange follow-up.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because advice alone is not the full brief intervention; the model continues with assistance and follow-up.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because assistance should not be deferred until after cessation has already occurred.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because redirecting to school performance does not address the requested vaping cessation support.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because repeating advice without offering support does not complete the brief intervention model.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
